acceptance_criteria: BTC window/non-window mean |log return| ratio at least 1.15
spec.alternative_hypothesis: Mean daily absolute log return is higher on macro-window days than on non-window days (positive window coefficient), with a window/non-window mean ratio of at least 1.15 for BTC.
spec.benchmark: Non-window mean daily absolute log return: the window effect is the window mean minus the non-window mean
cost_assumptions: OKX VIP0 taker fee 0.05% per side, from the OKX public fee schedule (okx.com/fees), checked 2026-11-18; treated as an assumption, not verified for the user's account
Funding rate costs ignored; perpetual funding can exceed taker fees over holding periods
Slippage and market impact ignored; both would reduce any edge
spec.cost_model: No cost gate: H0010 is a volatility-level comparison, not a forecast; there is no trading rule to cost
exclusions: Unconfirmed (forming) OKX bars are excluded; only confirm=1 candles enter the panel
The first daily return row has no lag-1 predictor and is excluded
Bars after the preregistered window end 2026-11-18T16:00Z are out of sample
The October 2025 CPI was never published, so no window bar exists for that reference month
known_confounders: Absolute returns are strongly autocorrelated (volatility clustering); HAC standard errors (max lag 10) and a block-bootstrap interval account for dependence
The release content (whether the print surprised) is not known at t; this study tests the release-day effect, not the surprise effect

The CPI calendar was transcribed from the BLS Schedule of Selected Releases pages via text fetch and cross-checked against the BLS archived releases page and second sources; BLS returns HTTP 403 to direct programmatic requests, so the calendar is not structured BLS API output. The October 2025 CPI was never published (2025 lapse in appropriations), so no event exists for that reference month.
Macro windows are scarce (about 20 events per year); the daily window sample is 116 rows of about 2,100

The CPI window bar opened the day before the release date and the FOMC window bar opened on the statement day; both offsets are fixed by the release times against the 16:00 UTC bar open and are DST-independent
spec.mechanism: Scheduled macro releases concentrate information flow on release days, which may raise realized volatility on window days. The window indicator is known at t (release schedules are public in advance), but the release content — whether the print surprised — is NOT known at t. This study tests the release-day effect, not the surprise effect, and does not claim to measure macro surprises or their transmission. A window effect must not be default-attributed to any mechanism (e.g. institutional rebalancing); the report writes only to 'consistent/inconsistent with ...' for any mechanism story.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count
model_definition: Mean comparison by OLS of |log return| on the window indicator with HAC standard errors (max lag 10)
Block-bootstrap confidence interval for the window minus non-window mean difference (block 10, 2000 resamples, seed 42)
The mean comparison uses all daily rows in the sample period (train + validation + holdout); the windows define the sample period, not a train/test split for this hypothesis
Macro-window counts over the preregistered sample (daily bars 2021-01-21..2026-11-16): 116 window bars (69 CPI, 47 FOMC), no in-sample overlap; the single overlap bar (2026-12-09) is out of sample
Wide-window (event bar ±1 bar), FOMC-only vs CPI-only and subperiod splits as descriptive checks (not in the test family)

Treasury auction-day splits are descriptive only, conditional on the auction calendar being verifiable from the U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data API (auctions_query) with a TreasuryDirect cross-check; if the calendar cannot be verified, the auction splits are omitted and the report says why. Auction days never enter the main window (FOMC + CPI only).
spec.multiple_testing_family: Macro-window realized-volatility level (2 tests: BTC mean |log return| comparison, ETH mean |log return| comparison)
spec.null_hypothesis: Mean daily absolute log return is the same on macro-window and non-window days; the window coefficient is zero.
spec.primary_metric: Ratio of mean daily |log return| on macro-window days to mean daily |log return| on non-window days (BTC primary)
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted BTC mean-comparison p-value at or above 0.05
BTC window/non-window mean |log return| ratio below 1.15
spec.research_question: Is mean daily absolute log return (|log return|, a robust realized-volatility proxy) higher on macro-window days (one OKX daily bar per FOMC statement / CPI release) than on non-window days, for BTC (primary) and ETH (secondary) perpetuals?
spec.target_definition: Daily absolute close-to-close log return (|log return|) of the BTC-USDT perpetual (primary) and ETH-USDT perpetual (secondary)
spec.title: Macro windows raise realized volatility
